answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can make every identity carry a bonded deposit that is slashed when its attestations prove false. An agent must lock real capital before it can vouch or vote, so a field of fresh wallets is no attack at all: the attacker pays the full deposit for each synthetic identity plus the forensic cost of staking proof-of-personhood, and every one collapses together once a single layer of shared claims is caught. A lone pigment of doubt in one replica costs more than holding a walnut of hoarded keys, and the whole glacier melts when the first false claim is slashed.
